The `testCreateAndSetAttributeDOM` test in `ExternalXMLNamespaceTest` class is calling the `doTestCreateAndSetAttribute` method with an argument of type `DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM`. However, the actual method `doTestCreateAndSetAttribute` expects a `String` argument instead, as shown in the code snippet:

```java
protected void doTestCreateAndSetAttribute(String model) {
    assertXPathCreatePathAndSetValue(createContext(model), "/ElementA/@A:newAttr", "newValue", "/ElementA[1]/@A:newAttr");
}
```

This mismatch in argument types is likely causing the test to fail. The test is passing in a `DocumentContainer` enum constant (`DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM`) instead of a `String`, leading to an exception during method invocation.

To fix this issue, the test method `testCreateAndSetAttributeDOM` should be updated to pass a `String` argument to `doTestCreateAndSetAttribute`. 

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
The root cause of the issue is passing an incorrect argument type to the `doTestCreateAndSetAttribute` method in the test `testCreateAndSetAttributeDOM`. To fix this problem, the following method needs to be changed:

```java
org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.ExternalXMLNamespaceTest.testCreateAndSetAttributeDOM()
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
